conformance.note: The 15-fixture conformance corpus. The M6 oracle criterion counts exactly these.

benchmark.note: Large real-world PDFs named by M2 acceptance. Not part of the oracle count.

engine.note: CC0 fixtures authored in this repo, for behaviours the Ethos corpus does not cover. Never counted toward the 15-fixture oracle criterion.

The ' and " show-text operators. " is absent from pdf-inspector's operator match, so its text vanishes silently and adjacent runs merge with corrupt geometry (checklist P6). Three runs expected, one per operator (M3).
Tz horizontal scaling, which pdf-inspector implements nowhere. The same string at Tz 100 and Tz 50 must produce advances in exactly a 2:1 ratio (M3).
A TJ adjustment of -500 thousandths: a word gap the document never wrote as a space glyph. The inserted space must be flagged at the character (M3).
Carries a /FontDescriptor with Ascent 718 / Descent -207, so the MEASURED ink path is exercised. Every other fixture takes the typed-absence path (M3).

Carries a /FontDescriptor that RESOLVES and answers nothing — no /Ascent, no /Descent, no /FontBBox, no embedded program — so resolve_font_ink walks the descriptor and still declines to measure. That route is what only this fixture covers: the three M3 engine fixtures also pair a known advance with absent geometry, but they carry no descriptor at all, and synthetic/simple-text never reaches the metrics branch because its advance is unknown too. /Widths IS supplied here, so the advance is known and the absence is attributable to the font's silence about ink extent alone. Drives the M5 geometry-omission path.

Carries an /Encoding whose /Differences remap codes 200-202 to glyph names no vendored table resolves, so those codes cannot be decoded at all. In WinAnsiEncoding the same three codes are E-grave/E-acute/E-circumflex, so a reader that ignored /Differences — or fell back to the base encoding on a glyph-name miss — would emit mojibake the document does not contain, inside a perfectly well-formed artifact. A reader substituting U+FFFD would be no better. v0.1 drops the affected run whole, keeps the decodable run, and declares broken-font-encoding with the count (parity checklist P10).

The v1-S1 ruled-table golden. A 3x3 lattice DRAWN with stroked `re` rectangles, one cell merged across columns 1-2 and one cell deliberately left empty. Two properties are the point: the merge makes CellSlot occupancy do real work (a cell spanning two columns must own both slots, which the shipped Ethos ODL adapter does not), and the empty cell is the fabrication-0 case (rectangles enclosing no text must yield empty text, never a neighbour's). Authored because the Ethos conformance corpus contains NO path operators at all -- `synthetic/table-regular-grid` lays its grid out with text position alone, so the ruled detector has nothing there to run on.

The v1-S1 cross-check hostile. Two rectangles claim the same lattice face, so the structural CellSlot cover cannot be exact and the geometric derivation sees an overlap. The engine must REPORT the disagreement on the artifact and never nudge a coordinate to make the grid tile (docs/01-CONTRACT.md 5.4).

v1-S2 NEAR MISS. Three rows, two columns, no path operators — and on the last row the right column sits at x=205 instead of 200. Five points is past the 150 centipoints the alignment rule folds together and under the 1200 it requires between two real columns, so the origins imply three column lines, two of them half a gutter apart. Expect `tables: []` plus a named refusal: rounding 205 back to 200 would move a coordinate a reader had no way to know was moved.

v1-S2 WHICH-RULE-FIRED. One page carrying a 2x2 grid the document PAINTS with `re` and a separate 2x2 grid implied by text alignment alone. Expect two tables, one `ruled-rects-v1` and one `unruled-align-v1`. The profile says which rules ran; only a per-table field can say which one found a given table.

v1-S2 ARBITRATION. A painted 2x2 grid whose four runs are also a flawless 2x2 alignment, so both rules can describe the region and exactly one may. Expect ONE table, `ruled-rects-v1`: a ruling line is evidence the author left, an alignment cluster is a decision this engine made, and the two grids are never averaged into a third nobody found.

v1-S3 STRUCTURAL-LOCATOR GOLDEN. Five runs, four locator states: mcid 0 and 1 are cited by the /StructTreeRoot (role path Document/P), mcid 5 is marked and claimed by nothing, one run sits inside an /Artifact sequence, and one is never marked at all. Collapsing any two of those would lose a real distinction — 'outside the tree', 'not marked', and 'marked as furniture' are three different statements. The artifact run stays in `nodes`, flagged and never dropped.

v1-S3 /RoleMap. The document maps its custom /Para onto /P and says nothing about /Odd. The mapped element gains a standard_role_path; the unmapped one keeps its own name and gains nothing. Deciding /Odd 'must mean' /P because it sits where a paragraph would is the inference this slice refuses.

v1-S3 TAGGED-VS-GEOMETRIC, agreeing. A painted 2x2 grid whose four cells are also tagged /TD under /Table/TR. The two derivations share no input — the tree walk reads no box and the detector reads no /S — so `ok` here is two independent readings arriving at one grid.

v1-S3 TAGGED-VS-GEOMETRIC, hostile. Same painted 2x2 and same four marked cells; the tree claims THREE rows, the third citing content the page never wrote. Expect a mismatch naming the row disagreement, `structure-item-without-content` for the two uncited items, and the detector's 2x2 left exactly as it was — no repair, and no run invented to satisfy the tree.

v1-S3 FAIL-CLOSED. /K points back at an ancestor. Walking it does not terminate and stopping partway would report a structure the document does not have, so extraction refuses with a named `malformed` error and produces no artifact.

v1-S4 FORM GOLDEN. One text field whose /V is a string NO Tj on the page draws — the page prints only the label beside it. Expect one form_field node carrying the value and NO text_run containing any fragment of it: a reader that copied widget values into the text layer, as LiteParse does, would be caught here (checklist L13).

v1-S4 ANNOTATION GOLDEN. A /Text annot whose /Contents must never appear among the runs, plus a second annot with /F bit 2 (hidden). Expect two annotation nodes: the hidden one is FLAGGED and KEPT, because honouring a rendering instruction by deleting content is an undeclared edit (checklist O21). Re-pinned at v1-S6.1: its catalog carried a spurious `/StructTreeRoot 6 0 R` pointing at THIS FIXTURE'S ANNOTATION dictionary, spliced by a heuristic in the generator rather than by intent. The fixture is about annotations and declares no structure tree now, so it reports `untagged-structure-tree-absent` as it always should have.

v1-S4 NO-REPAIR. A widget naming /Parent 9 0 R, an object the file does not contain. LiteParse repairs this in memory; expect instead the widget emitted with what it declares about itself, `form-field-parent-unresolved` on the wire, and the source bytes untouched. The field name is visibly shorter than the form intends rather than papered over.
v1-S4 XFA. An /AcroForm carrying /XFA beside a static field. Expect `xfa-forms-not-extracted` declared, the static sibling's value still read, and no attempt to parse the XML packet (checklist L15).

v1-S5 anti-cliff pair, half one. Two columns of seven lines, written RIGHT column first. Fourteen lines is one side of pdf-inspector's `min_lines < 15` boundary. Expect column-major order (L1..L7 then R1..R7) under `gutter-columns-v1`, and no table: the emission is not row-major, so the alignment rule refuses.

v1-S5 anti-cliff pair, half two. The SAME page with ONE line added to the left column. Fifteen lines is the other side of the boundary a line-count rule flips on. Expect the SAME column-major order, which is the whole point: the rule measures a gutter, and a gutter does not move when a line is added.

v1-S6 image golden. A 2x2 /FlateDecode image XObject PAINTED with `Do` under `120 0 0 60 40 60 cm`. Expect one image node whose rect is the MATRIX (120x60 points at (40,60)) and not the pixel count (2x2), a digest over the encoded stream, and media type `pdf_encoded_samples` — deflated samples are not a file. NO fixture in either owned corpus contains an image XObject, so without this the whole image path is untested.

v1-S6, the other half of the images proof. The SAME image object declared in /Resources and never drawn. Expect ZERO image nodes with the capability still true: `Do` is what makes a placement. Classify still counts the declared resource and reports `embedded-images`, which is a different question honestly answered.

v1-S6 hidden-text golden, and checklist O21 in one page. Three strings, the middle one under `3 Tr`. Expect all three PRESENT in reading order, the middle one flagged `invisible-render-mode`, and the count declared. A reader that filtered it would return a page that looks clean — the OpenDataLoader defect.

v1-S6 off-page golden, and the coordinate-repair golden. /MediaBox [0 20 300 220] — an origin that is NOT (0,0), which no document in either corpus has — plus /CropBox [0 40 300 200] and one run below it. Expect y=10000 and y=19000 (the origin is subtracted, which it was not through v1-S5) and exactly the second run flagged `off-page`, measured against the CROP box rather than the media box.

v1-S6 two-frame golden. /CropBox [50 50 250 150] strictly inside /MediaBox [0 0 300 200], a font with REAL ink metrics, and text at y=180 in the margin the crop box removes. Expect an artifact: page dimensions come from the MEDIA box, which is the frame every coordinate is expressed in. Reporting the crop box's size instead makes `seal` refuse the artifact — a measured box outside its declared page — so a cropping document stops parsing entirely. The only fixture where a MEASURED box lies outside the crop box.

v1-S6.1 golden, and the shape ZERO fixtures had before it. A TrueType font — SIMPLE, so its codes are one byte by PDF 32000-1 9.6 — carrying a /ToUnicode whose codespace declares TWO. Expect the text `Hi there` and NO font limitation. Split by the /ToUnicode codespace instead of by the font's declared kind, the codes fuse into pairs, none is in the map, and the run is dropped while the artifact blames the document's encoding — which is what happened to 8,417 runs of cfpb-home-loan-toolkit for six slices. Every conformance font is a Type1 with no /ToUnicode, so none of them could catch it.
